value.rationale: Conservation comparison asks whether changing a shared extinction threat can reverse rankings of two alternative phylogenetic histories more than once. The sharp eleven-leaf barrier and the full first exceptional response-profile layer are natural, nontrivial finite structural facts. The two exact crossing parameters make failure of monotone pairwise ranking concrete, while the all-n grafting result clarifies persistence beyond the cutoff. No biological data or generalized unequal-length claim is inferred.
